title: RTX 5070 Ti vs RX 9070: Which 1440p GPU to Buy in 2026
seo_title: RTX 5070 Ti vs RX 9070: Best 1440p GPU 2026 | Grey PC
meta_description: RTX 5070 Ti vs RX 9070: the 5070 Ti wins at ray tracing and DLSS 4, the RX 9070 wins on value and heat. Plus PSU sizing, CPU pairing and who should buy each.
excerpt: The RTX 5070 Ti vs RX 9070 choice comes down to ray tracing and DLSS 4 against value and lower power draw. Here is which 1440p card suits which buyer.
featured_image_alt: NVIDIA RTX 5070 Ti and AMD Radeon RX 9070 graphics cards side by side for a 1440p comparison
content_html:
In the rtx 5070 ti vs rx 9070 matchup, the RTX 5070 Ti is the faster card at 1440p, especially with ray tracing, while the RX 9070 costs less and draws noticeably less power. Buy the 5070 Ti if you want high refresh 1440p with ray tracing for years; buy the RX 9070 if you play mostly without ray tracing and want the best value. Both have 16 GB of VRAM, so neither will run out of memory soon.

Below we compare them on performance, features, power, cooling and who each card suits.

Note the pricing tier. The RTX 5070 Ti’s natural rival is the RX 9070 XT, not the plain RX 9070. This comparison matters because the RX 9070 often lands much closer in price to the cheaper RTX 5070, so many buyers end up choosing between a stretch and a saving.

Performance at 1440p

Without ray tracing, the RTX 5070 Ti is faster, but the gap is smaller than the price difference suggests. The RX 9070 delivers high frame rates in most current games at 1440p high settings, and in esports titles both cards exceed what most 165 Hz monitors can show.

With ray tracing on, the gap widens. NVIDIA’s ray tracing hardware and DLSS 4 give the 5070 Ti a clear lead in path-traced and heavily ray-traced games. RDNA 4 improved AMD’s ray tracing a lot over the previous generation, but it still trails in the heaviest workloads.

At 4K, the 5070 Ti is the more capable card, and it pairs well with DLSS. The RX 9070 can play at 4K with FSR 4, but it is better treated as a 1440p card.

Upscaling and Frame Generation

DLSS 4 is the 5070 Ti’s biggest advantage. It is supported in a very large number of games, its image quality is excellent, and multi frame generation can multiply frame rates in supported titles. It works best when the base frame rate is already reasonable; it does not fix a game running at 30 FPS.

FSR 4 is a big step up for AMD. It uses machine learning, like DLSS, and the image quality is now close. The catch is game support: fewer titles offer FSR 4 than DLSS, though the list keeps growing.

Power, Heat and Bahrain Summers

This is where the RX 9070 earns its place. At around 220 W it draws roughly 80 W less than the 5070 Ti. In a Bahrain room that already sits above 30 C for months, that is less heat dumped into the case, quieter fans, and a smaller power supply.

The RTX 5070 Ti is not hard to cool, but it needs a case with real airflow: a mesh front, at least two intake fans and a rear exhaust. Pick a card with a large triple-fan cooler. For small cases or rooms without strong air conditioning, the RX 9070 is the safer choice.

Power supply sizing follows the same logic. A quality 650 W Gold unit handles an RX 9070 build; give the 5070 Ti a 750 W unit with a native 12V-2x6 connector. Browse options on our PSU page.

Creative Work and Streaming

For video editing, 3D rendering and streaming, the RTX 5070 Ti is the stronger pick. NVIDIA’s NVENC encoder, CUDA support in Blender and DaVinci Resolve, and wider plugin support make it the default for creators.

The RX 9070’s encoder improved in RDNA 4 and is fine for streaming, but if your work depends on CUDA software, buy NVIDIA. See creator-ready systems on our workstation page.

Which CPU to Pair With Each Card

Both cards pair well with a Ryzen 5 9600X or Ryzen 7 9700X at 1440p. If you chase very high frame rates in competitive shooters, the Ryzen 7 9800X3D gets the most out of the 5070 Ti. Pair either card with 32 GB of DDR5-6000. Compare processors on our CPU page.

Buying in Bahrain

Both cards come in many partner versions, and prices vary with cooler size, factory overclock and stock. The spread between the cheapest and most expensive models of the same GPU can be large, and the extra money rarely buys more than a few percent of performance. A good mid-range cooler is the sweet spot.

Buying locally gives you a warranty you can actually use and a shop that can test the card in your system. Check current models and stock on our graphics card page, or ask Grey PC to build a full gaming PC around either card.

One more practical point: resale and longevity. Both cards have 16 GB of VRAM and current upscaling, so either should handle new 1440p releases for several years. If you upgrade often, NVIDIA cards tend to hold resale value a little better in the Gulf market. If you keep a card until it dies, the RX 9070’s lower power and heat make it an easy card to live with.

The Bottom Line

For the rtx 5070 ti vs rx 9070 decision, buy the RTX 5070 Ti if you want the best 1440p experience with ray tracing, DLSS 4 and creator features, and your case and PSU can handle 300 W. Buy the RX 9070 if you want strong 1440p performance for less money, lower power draw and an easier time in Bahrain’s heat. Both have 16 GB of VRAM and will age well.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the RTX 5070 Ti better than the RX 9070 at 1440p?

Yes, the RTX 5070 Ti is faster at 1440p, and the lead grows with ray tracing on. Without ray tracing the RX 9070 is closer than the price gap suggests and still delivers high frame rates. If you rarely use ray tracing, the RX 9070 gives better value; if you do, the 5070 Ti is worth it.

What PSU do I need for the RTX 5070 Ti vs RX 9070?

Use a quality 750 W 80 Plus Gold power supply for the RTX 5070 Ti, ideally with a native 12V-2x6 cable. The RX 9070 runs comfortably on a quality 650 W Gold unit. Spending a little more on a reputable PSU protects every other part in the PC and keeps fan noise low.

Does the RX 9070 have enough VRAM for 2026 games?

Yes. The RX 9070 has 16 GB of VRAM, the same amount as the RTX 5070 Ti. That is enough for high texture settings at 1440p in current games and leaves headroom for the next few years. The 5070 Ti’s GDDR7 memory is faster, but the capacity is identical.

Is DLSS 4 a reason to choose the RTX 5070 Ti over the RX 9070?

For many buyers, yes. DLSS 4 has wider game support than FSR 4, excellent image quality and multi frame generation. FSR 4 has closed much of the quality gap, but fewer games support it. If you play many new releases with upscaling on, DLSS 4 is a real advantage.

Which runs cooler in Bahrain, the RTX 5070 Ti or the RX 9070?

The RX 9070. It draws around 220 W against roughly 300 W for the RTX 5070 Ti, so it puts less heat into the case and room. In Bahrain’s summer that means quieter fans and lower temperatures. The 5070 Ti still runs well in a case with strong airflow.
